newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-SCOTTISH OPEN DROPPED FROM EUROPEAN TOUR.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-SCOTTISH OPEN DROPPED FROM EUROPEAN TOUR.

text.p: The Scottish Open golf tournament has been dropped from next season's European Tour schedule in favour of the Loch Lomond World Invitational tournament.
The Loch Lomond event will be staged in July, a week before the British Open championship at Scotland's Royal Troon.
"The week prior to the Open is a prime date in the schedule and traditionally has provided competition in Scotland," the Tour's executive director Ken Schofield said.
"Next year the Loch Lomond World Invitational will occupy the date at what is surely one of the most glorious settings in golf."

The Scottish Open, held every season since 1985, has struggled since losing its prime sponsor two years ago. Prize money at this year's event at Carnoustie was 480,000 pounds ($765,000) -- down from 650,000 pounds ($1.0 million) last year.
The prize fund for the Loch Lomond tournament, staged for the first time last month, was 780,000 pounds ($1.2 million).
